title: What is known about 1RB0LF_0RC0RB_1LC1LD_1RE0RD_---0RA_1LA0LF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LF_0RC0RB_1LC1LD_1RE0RD_---0RA_1LA0LF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves (kernel) that a halt needs a D-run (halt_needs_drun) and proves exact cycle rules of the particle dynamics (cycleP, for all values of their parameters). In the run, D-runs happened only four times, all in the first 2.4·106 steps and all at the wall at the right end. No halt in the first 1011 steps (C); the twin 1RB0RA_1LC0RA_0LD0LC_1RD1RE_1LF0LE_---0LB runs the same tape with one extra 1 at the wall.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: D with 1 under the head, 0 right, 0 two right. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: A halt needs a D-run
claims.text: Two steps before a halt the head is in state D reading a 1: E (the halting state, on a 0) is entered only from D0, and D from C1 (then E reads the 1 that C wrote) or from D1.

claims.title: One cycle with a P particle first
claims.text: From 0^inf F> 0010010111 0 01 (0101)^(x+4) 001011 (1010)^y R the machine reaches the same shape with x+3 and y+3 in 40x+330 steps, for every x, y and every tape R: the left gadget moves 8 cells left, P (001011) 12.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: Direct C simulation (c/deep.c), which also records how far right the head gets in each doubling of the step count.

claims.title: Only four D-runs in 10<sup>9</sup> steps, all at the wall
claims.text: At steps 130, 309, 2,306,898 and 2,380,763 D erased the wall block 1^6 at the right end; the block after it saved the machine each time.

claims.title: The twin runs the same tape plus one 1
claims.text: 1RB0RA_1LC0RA_0LD0LC_1RD1RE_1LF0LE_---0LB is this machine mirrored, with states renamed, started in state F; at all 32,539 left-end records of the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps its tape equals this one plus one 1 at the end of the wall, and its step count is 56 more (constant since step 4,194,242).

claims.title: Particles and their speeds
claims.text: Sampled once per cycle of the left gadget, the junctions (00, 11) of the tape form 11 to 15 small clusters whose displacements per cycle are constants (gadget 8 cells, o 4, P 12, Q 8); the head only reaches the far particles when the near ones are used up, like a carry. Read off samples, not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Open. It would need a trip of the head that reaches the wall and finds it in a shape where the D-run ends on 00. An exact macro machine for the particles is the next step.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0RA_1LC0RA_0LD0LC_1RD1RE_1LF0LE_---0LB up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

check: cd holdouts/1RB0LF_0RC0RB_1LC1LD_1RE0RD_---0RA_1LA0LF && gcc -O2 -o snap c/snap.c && ./snap 1RB0LF_0RC0RB_1LC1LD_1RE0RD_---0RA_1LA0LF 3000000 4 > s.txt && python3 py/particles.py s.txt

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. This machine keeps almost all of its tape as a plain 1010... pattern that its head flips back and forth without changing anything; what matters are a dozen small defects, particles, that a little counter at the left end pushes around one at a time, like carries. Lean proves the machine can only halt in a rare event that, so far, has only happened at the far right wall of the tape, four times, early on.

facts.text: A halt needs D erasing 1s (Lean, kernel); D-runs have only happened at the wall.
Exact cycles of the particle dynamics, for all parameters (Lean, kernel).
No halt in the C simulator.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.516). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 65,134 cells (49,805 left of the start, 56 right), with a density of 1s of 0.525.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A sea with particles
html: Stop the machine at almost any moment and the tape is 1010101010... nearly everywhere. Call a junction a place where two equal cells touch (00 or 11). Junctions are rare and come in small clusters: the particles. Between them lie long stretches of the alternating sea.

The trick of this machine: when the head crosses the sea, in either direction, it complements every cell (0 becomes 1, 1 becomes 0). Moving left, F turns 1s into 0s and on a 0 writes a 1 and passes to A, which turns the next 1 into a 0 and passes back to F. Moving right, a six-step zig-zag of C, D, E, A, B does the same four cells at a time. Complementing an alternating pattern gives an alternating pattern, and it does not move the junctions. So the head can cross any amount of sea without changing anything that matters; the whole state of the machine is the list of particles and the distances between them.

At the left end sits a small gadget (0 0 1 0 0 1 0 1 1 1 0), at the right end a wall of 1s (1^6 0 1^4). In between, after 109 steps, 11 to 15 particles; the seas between them are thousands of cells long.

sections.heading: The gadget counts to four, then sends the head deep
html: The head returns to the left end four times per cycle. Three of those trips are short (22, 34 and 22 steps): they only flip the gadget through its states, like the low bits of a counter. The fourth trip is deep: the head runs right across the sea until a particle turns it back. Every return to the left end adds two cells, so the tape grows by 8 cells per cycle on the left.
When the first particle is P = 0 0 1 0 1 1, one cycle does exactly this (Lean, cycleP, for all x and y):

The gadget moves 8 cells left, P moves 12 cells left, so the sea between them shrinks by 4 cells per cycle and the sea behind P grows by 12. The rest of the tape, R, is never looked at. After x cycles P reaches the gadget, they collide, new particles come out, and the deep trips go further.

sections.heading: The particles
html: Sampled once per cycle, the particles keep their shape for long stretches and each moves a fixed number of cells per cycle when the deep trip reaches it:

particlecellsmoves per cycle
gadget0 0 1 0 0 1 0 1 1 1 08 left (the tape grows)
o0 04 left
P0 0 1 0 1 112 left, when the trip ends there
QP followed by a train (1 0 1 1)^k8 left; the train grows by two words
Rtwo forms that alternate4 left
Tstretches of the second sea 1110 1110 ...8 left

The far particles are only reached when the near ones have been used up, the way a carry reaches the high digits of a counter only rarely. That is why the tape grows like the square root of the step count: each cycle costs a trip across a tape that keeps getting longer.

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The machine stops when E reads a 0. E is entered only from D reading a 0; D is entered either from C reading a 1 (C writes 1, moves left, and then E would read that very 1: no halt) or from D reading a 1. So two steps before a halt, D must be erasing a block of 1s to its right (Lean, halt_needs_drun), and the halt comes if that block ends in 0 0.

Such a D-run starts when C, moving left, meets two 1s side by side. In the sea and among the particles that never happens. In the first 109 steps there were exactly four D-runs, at steps 130, 309, 2,306,898 and 2,380,763: each time a trip had carried all the way to the right end and D erased the wall block 1^6; the block of 1s after it saved the machine. Since step 8.4·106 no trip has come near the wall.
So the question is whether some future carry reaches the wall and finds it in a fatal shape. Nobody knows.

sections.heading: The same table, twice on the list
html: 1RB0RA_1LC0RA_0LD0LC_1RD1RE_1LF0LE_---0LB is this machine seen in a mirror, with the states renamed, started in this machine's state F. Its first step writes a 1 and lands in this machine's state A, so it runs this machine from a tape with one extra 1. That 1 ends up at the end of the wall and stays there: at every one of the 32,539 left-end records of the first 109 steps the two tapes agree except for that 1, and the twin is always 56 steps ahead.

sections.heading: What is proved
html: Lean, kernel: halt_needs_drun (lean/Halt.lean); the cycle rule cycleP (lean/Rules.lean, written by py/gen_rules.py with bbtools.symtm); no halt in 104 steps. native_decide: no halt in 107 steps. C: no halt in 1011 steps; the D-runs and the twin comparison over 109 steps. Heuristic: the particle table. Open: the exact particle machine and the halting question.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0RA_1LC0RA_0LD0LC_1RD1RE_1LF0LE_---0LB: rename A→B, B→C, C→D, D→E, E→F, F→A and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state F, in a mirror

summary: The tape is a sea of 1010 carrying a dozen particles that a 2-bit gadget at the left end pushes around like a counter with carries; a halt needs a D-run, and D-runs have only happened when a rare trip reached the wall at the right end.
